fullPassage:
Save Coral Reefs

When you go deep into the sea, you can see a variety of marine animals including corals. Over the course of many years, corals build up to form large structures called coral reefs. Brightly colored coral reefs provide a beautiful underwater landscape. However, this is not the only reason they are valuable.

Importance of Coral Reefs

Coral reefs are crucial ecosystems that protect both marine life and people living near the sea. Coral reefs provide shelter to an abundance of marine life, such as fish and underwater plants. Because of the diversity of life found in coral reefs, they are often called "the rainforests of the sea." Nearly one quarter of all known marine species depend on coral reefs for survival — they hide themselves from predators, find food, reproduce, and raise their young in coral reefs.

As far as humans are concerned, over half a billion people rely on coral reefs for safety and survival. When large waves generated by storms rush toward shore, coral reefs serve as natural barriers. The force of the waves is reduced as they hit the coral reefs. Consequently, they prevent the land on the shore from washing away and thus protect towns near the sea. Moreover, reefs are a source of medicine, and many organisms found in coral reefs are used to treat diseases like cancer. This is why they are sometimes referred to as the "medicine chests of the sea."

Coral Reefs in Danger

These underwater treasures are under threat of destruction. The more coral reefs become damaged, the more creatures relying on them will lose their homes. Thus, the increasing loss of coral reefs might lead to the destruction of the entire marine ecosystem. The U.N. reported that many of the world's coral reefs are currently endangered. In fact, nearly half of Australia's Great Barrier Reef, the world's largest, has disappeared. If swift action is not taken, scientists estimate that most coral reefs will be destroyed by 2050.

What causes coral reefs to die? There are various causes, like destructive fishing techniques, overpopulation of corals' natural enemies, and careless tourism. However, the leading cause is the rise in water temperature due to global warming. The ideal temperature range for corals to live is 20°C to 28°C. When the water temperature rises above 30°C, coral reefs turn white and eventually die. Another serious cause is plastic waste. Plastic products, such as bottles and fishing lines, have been dumped into the sea. This spreads viruses and diseases, damaging coral reefs and their inhabitants.

Technologies to Save Coral Reefs

In recent years, advanced technologies have been put in place to save coral reefs by monitoring, protecting, and restoring them in quick and efficient ways. Researchers from Florida introduced a soft jellyfish-like robot to monitor coral reefs without damaging their delicate bodies. In addition, an Australian research team invented an intelligent underwater robot to protect coral reefs from a dangerous species of starfish. The robot uses a camera and computerized vision system to scan the reefs and identify this starfish. When it encounters one, the robot uses a foldable arm to inject some toxic salt into the starfish and eliminate it. Meanwhile, 3D printing systems have been proposed in Hong Kong as one way to restore coral reef structures. The 3D printer creates artificial support for corals. An example is a block made of mud that lies on the floor of the ocean. It is shaped in a way that allows corals to attach to it and grow easily.

Actions to Save Coral Reefs

Here are some simple but effective steps we can take in order to help protect coral reefs. First, you can avoid using beauty products containing tiny pieces of plastic because they pollute the oceans. Also, try not to use sunscreen made with certain chemicals that damage corals. Second, you can volunteer to help clean the beach. Recycling and reducing trash is a huge help in maintaining a clean ocean. Last but not least, make it known that coral reefs are in danger by spreading the word to people around you. Let people know about the threat to coral reefs and what actions to take to save them. This will make a big difference for the future.

questions.stem:
글의 흐름으로 보아 다음 문장이 들어갈 위치로 가장 적절한 곳은?

"Because of the diversity of life found in coral reefs, they are often called 'the rainforests of the sea.'"

det.korean: 다양한 해양 생물에게 보금자리 제공 → 다양성 때문에 열대우림이라 불림 → 구체적 수치(4분의 1).
det.analysis: ✅ ②: 보금자리 제공(구체적 예시) → 다양성으로 인한 별명 → 4분의 1이 의존(구체 수치). ❌ ①: 첫 문장 바로 뒤는 보금자리 설명이 먼저. ❌ ③④: 이미 구체 예시 후에 별명이 오면 어색.
det.tip: shelter → diversity → 'rainforests of the sea' → 4분의 1. 일반→구체 흐름.

questions.stem:
글의 흐름으로 보아 다음 문장이 들어갈 위치로 가장 적절한 곳은?

"In addition, an Australian research team invented an intelligent underwater robot to protect coral reefs from a dangerous species of starfish."

det.korean: 플로리다 해파리 로봇(모니터링) → 추가로 호주 로봇(보호) → 카메라/비전 시스템으로 스캔.
det.analysis: ✅ ②: 'In addition'이 플로리다 로봇 소개 뒤에 호주 로봇을 추가. 이후 'The robot'이 호주 로봇을 받아 설명. ❌ ①: 총론 바로 뒤에 호주 로봇이 오면 플로리다 로봇이 뒤로 밀림. ❌ ③④: 이미 호주 로봇의 행동 설명 중간/뒤에 소개 삽입은 어색.
det.tip: 'In addition'은 앞 내용에 추가 정보 도입. 'The robot'은 바로 앞에 소개된 호주 로봇을 지칭.

questions.passage: Nearly one quarter of all known marine species ①<u>depend</u> on coral reefs for survival — they hide ②<u>themselves</u> from predators, find food, ③<u>reproduce</u>, and raise their young in coral reefs. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 인간에 관해서는(concerned), 5억 명 이상이 산호초에 의존한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①depend: 복수주어 species(종) 정상. ✅ ②themselves: they의 재귀대명사. ✅ ③reproduce: 병렬 구조(hide, find, reproduce, raise). ❌ ④concerning: 'as far as ~ are concerned'가 올바른 관용 표현. concerning은 전치사('~에 관하여')로 다른 용법.
det.tip: as far as ~ is/are concerned: ~에 관한 한. concerned(과거분사) 필수.

questions.passage: Moreover, reefs are a source of medicine, and many organisms ①<u>found</u> in coral reefs are used to treat diseases like cancer. This is ②<u>why</u> they are sometimes referred to as the "medicine chests of the sea." These underwater treasures are under threat of ③<u>destruction</u>. The more coral reefs become ④<u>damaging</u>, the more creatures relying on them will lose their homes.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 산호초가 손상될수록(damaged), 더 많은 생물이 보금자리를 잃을 것이다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①found: 과거분사, organisms를 수식(수동). ✅ ②why: 'This is why ~' 관계부사. ✅ ③destruction: 명사, 전치사 of 뒤. ❌ ④damaging: 산호초가 '손상되는(수동)' 것이므로 damaged 필요.
det.tip: damaged(손상된, 수동/형용사) vs damaging(손상을 주는, 능동). 산호초가 손상을 '당하는' 것.

questions.passage: Here are some simple but effective steps we can take in order to help protect coral reefs. First, you can avoid ①<u>using</u> beauty products ②<u>containing</u> tiny pieces of plastic because they pollute the oceans. Also, try not to use sunscreen ③<u>making</u> with certain chemicals that damage corals. Last but not least, make it ④<u>known</u> that coral reefs are in danger by spreading the word to people around you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 특정 화학 물질로 만들어진(made) 자외선 차단제를 사용하지 말라.
det.analysis: ✅ ①using: avoid + V-ing 정상. ✅ ②containing: 현재분사, products를 수식(능동). ❌ ③making: sunscreen이 '만들어지는(수동)' 것이므로 made 필요. ✅ ④known: make it known 사역동사 구문 정상.
det.tip: made with ~(~로 만들어진, 수동) vs making(만드는, 능동). 자외선 차단제는 화학물질로 '만들어진' 것.

questions.passage: Coral reefs are crucial ecosystems that protect both marine life and people living near the sea. det.korean: 포식자로부터 숨고, 먹이를 찾고, 번식하고, 산호초에서 새끼를 기른다(raise).
det.analysis: ✅ ①shelter(보금자리): 원문 그대로. ✅ ②survival(생존): 원문 그대로. ✅ ③reproduce(번식하다): 원문 그대로. ❌ ④abandon(버리다): 원문은 raise(기르다). 새끼를 '버리는' 것은 반대.
det.tip: raise(기르다) ↔ abandon(버리다). raise their young = 새끼를 기르다.

questions.passage: In recent years, advanced technologies have been put in place to save coral reefs by monitoring, protecting, and restoring them in quick and ①<u>efficient</u> ways. Researchers from Florida introduced a soft jellyfish-like robot to ②<u>monitor</u> coral reefs without ③<u>damaging</u> their delicate bodies. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 호주 연구팀이 해로운 불가사리로부터 산호초를 보호하기(protect) 위해 로봇을 발명했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①efficient(효율적인): 원문 그대로. ✅ ②monitor(모니터링하다): 원문 그대로. ✅ ③damaging(손상시키다): 원문 그대로. ❌ ④endanger(위험에 빠뜨리다): 원문은 protect(보호하다). 산호초를 '위험에 빠뜨리기' 위해 로봇을 만든 건 반대.
det.tip: protect(보호하다) ↔ endanger(위험에 빠뜨리다). 로봇의 목적은 보호.

det.korean: 과학자들은 대부분의 산호초가 2050년까지 파괴될 것으로 추정한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③estimate: 데이터 기반 예측/추정. ❌ ①deny(부인): 반대 의미. ❌ ②guarantee(보장): 확실성 과도. ❌ ④celebrate(축하): 맥락 무관.
det.tip: estimate: 추정하다. 과학적 데이터에 기반한 예측.

questions.passage: What causes coral reefs to die? There are various causes, like destructive fishing techniques, overpopulation of corals' natural enemies, and careless tourism. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그러나 주된 원인은 지구 온난화로 인한 수온 상승이다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①leading: '주된, 으뜸가는'. However 전환 후 가장 중요한 원인 강조. ❌ ②minor(사소한): However 이후 강조와 모순. ❌ ③unlikely(가능성 낮은): 맥락 불일치. ❌ ④temporary(일시적인): 지구 온난화는 지속적.
det.tip: leading cause = main cause = primary cause: 주된 원인. 'However'로 다른 원인과 대비.

det.korean: 산호초에서 발견되는 많은 유기체는 암 같은 질병을 치료하는 데 사용된다.
det.analysis: Many organisms(주어) found in coral reefs(과거분사 후치수식) are used(수동태) to treat(to부정사) diseases like cancer.
det.tip: found(과거분사) = 수동 수식. are used to V = ~하는 데 사용되다. treat diseases = 질병을 치료하다.

questions.ans: Many organisms found in coral reefs are used to treat diseases like cancer.

questions.passage: Here are some simple but effective steps we can take in order to help protect coral reefs. First, you can avoid using beauty products containing tiny pieces of plastic because they pollute the oceans. Also, try not to use sunscreen made with certain chemicals that damage corals. Second, you can volunteer to help clean the beach. Recycling and reducing trash is a huge help in maintaining a clean ocean. Last but not least, make it known that coral reefs are in danger by spreading the word to people around you.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 미세 플라스틱이 포함된 미용 제품은 산호초에 유익하다.
해변 청소는 산호초 보호와 관련이 없다.
산호초의 위험을 주변 사람들에게 알리는 것이 도움이 된다.

det.korean: 주변 사람들에게 위험을 알리는 것(spreading the word)이 도움이 된다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④: 'make it known that coral reefs are in danger by spreading the word' 원문과 일치. ❌ ①: 미세 플라스틱은 바다를 오염시킴. ❌ ②: 'certain chemicals'이 포함된 것만 해로움. ❌ ③: 해변 청소는 보호 방법 중 하나.
det.tip: 모든(all) vs 특정(certain): 원문은 'certain chemicals'으로 한정.

questions.passage: As far as humans are concerned, over half a billion people rely on coral reefs for safety and survival. When large waves generated by storms rush toward shore, coral reefs serve as natural barriers. The force of the waves is reduced as they hit the coral reefs. Consequently, they prevent the land on the shore from washing away and thus protect towns near the sea. Moreover, reefs are a source of medicine, and many organisms found in coral reefs are used to treat diseases like cancer. This is why they are sometimes referred to as the "medicine chests of the sea."
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 약 50만 명의 사람들이 안전과 생존을 위해 산호초에 의존한다.
산호초는 폭풍에 의해 생긴 큰 파도에 대해 자연 장벽 역할을 한다.
산호초에서 발견되는 유기체는 암 같은 질병 치료에 사용된다.

det.korean: 50만(500,000)이 아니라 5억(half a billion = 500,000,000)이다.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ① '약 50만 명': 원문은 'over half a billion'(5억 이상). 50만으로 수치를 왜곡.
❌ ② 산호초는 자연 장벽 역할: 원문 그대로
❌ ③ 유기체가 암 치료에 사용: 원문 그대로
❌ ④ 바다의 약상자: 원문 그대로
det.tip: half a billion = 500,000,000 = 5억. half a million = 500,000 = 50만. billion vs million 구분 필수.

questions.passage: Another serious cause is plastic waste. Plastic products, such as bottles and fishing lines, have been dumped into the sea. This spreads viruses and diseases, damaging coral reefs and their inhabitants.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용을 바탕으로, 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 영어 표현을 2단어로 쓰시오. Plastic products have been __________ into the sea, which spreads viruses and diseases.
accept: DUMPED
Dumped
dumped

det.korean: 플라스틱 제품이 바다에 버려져(dumped) 바이러스와 질병을 퍼뜨린다.
det.analysis: 'Plastic products have been dumped into the sea.' → dumped. 수동태 현재완료.
det.tip: dump: 버리다, 투기하다. have been dumped = 버려져 왔다 (현재완료 수동태).
